28 The diagram shows a long rope fixed at one end. The other end is moved up and down, setting
up a stationary wave.
vibration

X

What is the phase difference between the oscillations at X and at Y?
A
0
B
45°
C
90°
D
135°

hints: Look at where the solid and dashed envelopes cross - those crossings are the nodes - and check whether X and Y lie in the same loop between two successive nodes.
Recall that in a stationary wave all particles between two adjacent nodes vibrate in phase with each other, while particles in neighbouring loops vibrate in antiphase.
Check the diagram at X and Y: when the rope is on the solid curve both are above equilibrium, and when it is on the dashed curve both are below, so compare their timing to find the phase difference.
walkthrough: Identify the stationary wave pattern: the solid line and dashed line are the two extreme positions, and where they cross the displacement is always zero - these are the nodes.
Locate X and Y on the diagram: both lie inside the same central loop, bounded on the left and right by the same pair of adjacent nodes.

State the stationary-wave rule: all points between two successive nodes oscillate in phase with the same frequency, reaching maxima, minima and zero at the same instants, while adjacent loops are $180^\circ$ out of phase.
Apply it here: at one instant both X and Y are on the upper solid curve, half a cycle later both are on the lower dashed curve, so their displacements always have the same sign and vary together.
Therefore the phase difference between X and Y is $0$, with no lead or lag. This is option A.

A.explanation: X and Y are in the same loop between the same two adjacent nodes, so they move up and down together in phase with phase difference $0$.

B.explanation: A progressive wave has phase changing gradually with distance, but in a stationary wave there is no $45^\circ$ shift for two points in the same loop.

C.explanation: A $90^\circ$ quarter-cycle shift does not occur here because X and Y reach maximum displacement and zero displacement at the same times.

D.explanation: A large shift such as $135^\circ$ would require points in different loops or a travelling wave, whereas X and Y are on the same vibrating segment.
